title: IMPLEMENTATION OF E-COURTS INTEGRATED MISSION MODE PROJECT
body_text:
The e-Courts Mission Mode Project is being implemented in a phased manner across the country with the objective of strengthening the use of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) in the judicial system. The ongoing Phase i.e. [Phase III (2023-27)] envisions a transition towards digital, paperless and more intelligent courts through large-scale digitisation of records, wider use of virtual hearings, deeper interoperability across justice institutions and adoption of emerging technologies including Artificial Intelligence (AI). The details of progress achieved under Phase – III of the project is at Annexure – I.
The implementation of the eCourts Mission Mode Project has improved case management through the Case Information System (CIS) 4.0 and the JustIS application, enabling Judges to digitally manage and monitor cases. It has strengthened digital filing through the e-Filing system, which facilitates online filing of cases and related applications, and e-Payments for online payment of court fees. Further, video conferencing facilities have enabled virtual and hybrid court hearings across the implemented courts. These initiatives have enhanced the efficiency, accessibility and transparency of judicial administration and service delivery.
Under the eCourts Mission Mode Project, various steps have been undertaken to improve digital literacy and awareness among litigants and lawyers, including those in Andhra Pradesh. These include training programmes, capacity-building workshops, user manuals, video tutorials and outreach initiatives conducted through the High Courts and the State Judicial Academies.
Further, eSewa Kendras assist litigants and advocates in registration on the e-Filing portal, scanning and uploading of petitions, online payment of court fees, case status enquiries, certified copy applications, video conferencing and access to other digital court services. In addition, the eCourts services, District Court websites and eCourts mobile application provide online access to case status, cause lists, judgments, orders and other court-related information. These initiatives promote digital literacy, enhance awareness and facilitate wider access to eCourts services.
Annexure-I
The details of progress achieved under eCourts Phase – III:

Expansion of the Virtual Courts for hearing of court cases by creating the robust digital infrastructure. 538 courts are equipped Digitisation of the entire court record - both legacy records and fresh filing of cases 753.60 crore pages digitised Implementation of e-filing of court case 4519 courts Provision for enhancing and upgrading the available infrastructure of Video Conferencing 7553 establishments have VC facilities including courts, jails and hospitals. Court room live audio-visual streaming system 11 High Courts Solar facilities for ensuring seamless availability of ICT infrastructure 1626 courts complexes are equipped Providing National Service & Tracking of electronic Processes (NSTEP) facility 6895 courts have NSTEP facility. Migration of all High Court and District Court websites to S3WAAS platform 734 courts sites migrated Additional hardware to courts and judicial officers in Phase II 18380 courts provided Integration with Inter-operable Criminal Justice System (ICJS) to enable seamless transfer of data and information among different pillars like courts, police, jails, forensic labs All High Courts have implemented ICJS Training of all stakeholders 2372 Trainings held Connectivity 174 Sites connected with Software Defined Wide Area Network (SDWAN) technology
This information was given by MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal in a written reply to a question in Rajya Sabha today.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Law and Justice provided a Rajya Sabha update on the eCourts Mission Mode Project, currently in Phase III (2023-27), which aims to build digital, paperless and AI-enabled courts. Key achievements include 1,806 fully functional eSewa Kendras, 753.60 crore pages of court records digitised, e-filing implemented in 4,519 courts, 7,553 establishments with video conferencing facilities, and integration of all High Courts with the Interoperable Criminal Justice System (ICJS). Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal also highlighted digital literacy initiatives for litigants and lawyers, including in Andhra Pradesh.
enrichment.context:
The eCourts Mission Mode Project, launched under the National e-Governance Plan and overseen by the e-Committee of the Supreme Court of India, seeks to transform India's judicial system through ICT to improve access to justice, reduce case pendency, and increase transparency. Phase I and II laid the groundwork with computerisation of district and subordinate courts, case information systems, and basic digital infrastructure; Phase III (2023-27) pushes toward paperless courts, AI adoption, virtual hearings, and deeper interoperability with allied justice institutions like police, prisons, and forensic labs via the Interoperable Criminal Justice System (ICJS).

This initiative is significant given India's massive judicial pendency (over 4-5 crore cases across courts) and long-standing concerns about access to justice, especially for litigants in remote areas. Tools like eSewa Kendras, e-filing, e-payment, and the NSTEP system for electronic process tracking aim to reduce procedural delays and physical dependency on court premises. The project also ties into India's broader digital governance push (Digital India) and reflects judicial reform efforts to leverage technology for speedier, more transparent dispute resolution, complementing other justice-sector reforms like fast-track courts and alternate dispute resolution mechanisms.

prelims_questions.question: The 'eCourts Mission Mode Project' in India is primarily implemented under the guidance of which body?
options: e-Committee of the Supreme Court of India
prelims_questions.explanation: The eCourts Mission Mode Project is implemented under the policy guidance of the e-Committee of the Supreme Court of India, in coordination with the Department of Justice, Ministry of Law and Justice.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of the eCourts Mission Mode Project as highlighted in its Phase III implementation?
options: National Service and Tracking of Electronic Processes (NSTEP)
Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) for legal aid disbursement
prelims_questions.explanation: DBT for legal aid disbursement is not a component mentioned under the eCourts Project; the release lists ICJS integration, NSTEP, and eSewa Kendras as key components of Phase III.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the role of the eCourts Mission Mode Project in improving judicial efficiency and access to justice in India. What challenges remain in achieving a fully digital and paperless judiciary?
Examine how the integration of the Interoperable Criminal Justice System (ICJS) with the eCourts platform can enhance coordination among various pillars of the criminal justice system in India.
